stories.headline: India's 3-part truce plan seen as 'broadest' for ending Russia-Ukraine war
stories.title: India's 3-part truce plan seen as 'broadest' for ending Russia-Ukraine war
stories.summary: The Geopolitical Monitor report highlights that New Delhi has proposed a three-part truce between Russia and Ukraine that would stop attacks on energy facilities and other infrastructure, ensure the continued flow of grain and energy through Black Sea ports, and end attacks on commercial ships.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Geopolitical Monitor report highlights that New Delhi has proposed a three-part truce between Russia and Ukraine that would stop attacks on energy facilities and other infrastructure, ensure the continued flow of grain and energy through Black Sea ports, and end attacks on commercial ships.

New Delhi: While US President Donald Trump’s efforts focus on building pressure on Russia and Ukraine not to strike each other's oil refineries, India seems to be involved in broader discussions aimed at achieving a more comprehensive cessation of hostilities, according to a report.

The proposal, conveyed to Ukrainian officials during External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar’s visit to Kyiv in September, goes beyond separate ceasefire initiatives put forward by Turkey, Egypt, and the United States and seeks to address both infrastructure and maritime security while maintaining vital commodity flows, states the report by Nikola Mikovic.
"We have four proposals.
The broadest is India’s proposal.

We are ready for an energy and Black Sea ceasefire, but only in this combination," the report cited Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha as saying, adding that an energy ceasefire would mean a complete halt to strikes on all energy facilities, including port infrastructure.
The remarks suggest that Kyiv is open to New Delhi’s broader diplomatic initiative.
Although the Kremlin also welcomed India’s efforts, Moscow described the plan as "addressing only one specific aspect of a potential settlement".

Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov also echoed US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s assessment that there were currently "no prospects for a diplomatic resolution to the war", arguing that the conditions for negotiations were "not yet in place".
Russia has repeatedly stressed that it is seeking only a "sustainable just peace", rather than a ceasefire.
From Moscow’s perspective, a truce would only give Ukraine time to regroup, rearm, and prepare for another round of fighting.

For Kyiv, under the current circumstances, an energy ceasefire alone, without a broader agreement addressing other aspects of the conflict, does not seem particularly useful either, the report stated.

stories.headline: Magnitude 3 earthquake strikes Madhya Pradesh
stories.title: Magnitude 3 earthquake strikes Madhya Pradesh
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Khargone: An earthquake of magnitude three struck the Khargone district of Madhya Pradesh on Sunday, according to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS).
According to NCS, the epicentre of the earthquake was located in the Khargone area at a depth of 5 kilometres around 12:15 pm.
"EQ of M: 3.0, On: 18/10/2026 12:15:23 IST, Lat: 21.483 N, Long: 75.953 E, Depth: 5 Km, Location: Khargone, Madhya Pradesh," NCS said in a post on platform X.
A day earlier, an earthquake struck Shimla in Himachal Pradesh in the early hours of Saturday, with tremors recorded at 4:36 AM, according to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS).
The magnitude 4.1 earthquake was recorded at Latitude 31.298 N, Longitude 77.529 E, at a Depth of 10 kilometres.
Earlier on October 6, earthquake tremors were felt across the Delhi-NCR region, with the epicentre of the quake located in Uttarakhand, according to the NCS.

stories.headline: Rajasthan High Court Denies Bail To Government Officials Accused Of Facilitating Fake Aadhaar Cards, Cites National Security Concerns
stories.title: Rajasthan High Court Denies Bail To Government Officials Accused Of Facilitating Fake Aadhaar Cards, Cites National Security Concerns
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'national security' in title weight 70
article_sentences: Rajasthan High Court rejected second bail applications of accused persons charged with compromising the sanctity of UIDAI (Aadhar Card Project) by assisting a person who was operating an Aadhar Card Enrollment/Updatation Centre which was not in accordance with the conditions of UIDAI.

The bail applicants were government officials, who were working as programmer and assistance programmer, who were accused of being involved in fabrication, manipulation, and preparing forged and false Aadhar cards which could be used in anti-national activities.

While rejecting the bail application, the bench of Justice Ashok Kumar Jain observed that Rajasthan was a bordering state to Pakistan, and in border areas, resignation and updation in Aadhar data gave rise to activities that might be prejudicial to national interest.

“The uniqueness of the project (Aadhar) reflect that it has become one identity across the country, and same is used largely for direct benefit transfer, but due to some black-sheeps, the project has been misused by some of them, and people have created fake identity for financial or otherwise gains.”

For context, the order passed by the single bench that rejected the first bail application of the applicants, highlighted that the applicants provided password of the Government Internet- Raj-SWAN (Rajasthan State Wide Area Network) to the person operating the unauthorized centre, compromising the sanctity of the UIDAI, and obtained monetary benefits for the same.
Accordingly, the Court rejected the bail application of the applicants, opining their acts to be serious and grave.

“These petitioners are government servants, and after considering their role and involvement, I am of considered view that the petitioners does not deserve any leniency, at least for the reason that they are supposed to not only prevent any misuse of technology, but also expected to remain vigilant about any information of commission of crime using Aadhar as base.”
Accordingly, the bail applications were rejected.

stories.headline: Menstrual hygiene: SC expresses displeasure over states, UTs not responding to Centre
stories.title: Menstrual hygiene: SC expresses displeasure over states, UTs not responding to Centre
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 18: The Supreme Court has expressed displeasure over states and Union territories not responding to the Centre on how its judgment declaring menstrual hygiene as a part of the fundamental right under Article 21 of the Constitution is being implemented. “If what we have said in the judgment is only going to remain on paper, how is the Union, states/UTs going to give effect to this fundamental right?” a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and R Mahadevan said. It said the apex court had declared menstrual hygiene/menstrual health as one of the facets of Article 21 of the Constitution, which deals with the protection of life and personal liberty. The bench said that on September 1, it had directed the states and UTs to take into consideration the deficiencies highlighted by it and report in that regard by the next date of hearing. In a significant judgment delivered on January 30, the apex court said that the right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution includes the right to menstrual health. During the hearing in the matter on October 13, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, told the bench that the Union of India has taken up this issue very seriously with all the states and UTs to respond in what manner the judgment is being implemented. “Unfortunately, the states/UTs have not responded to the Union so far. We fail to understand that once the Union calls for the necessary information, why the states/UTs do not respond,” the bench said. “We are sure that the Union, the states/UTs have realised the importance of the judgment that we delivered, declaring menstrual hygiene as a part of the fundamental right,” it said. The bench said the apex court's verdict was in the interest of young girls who were giving up education, more particularly, in remote parts of the country because of the problem of menstrual hygiene, etc. “We direct the Union to take up this issue very seriously with each state/UT and call for the necessary information in writing as to what steps they have taken so far for giving effect to the judgment delivered by this court,” it said. The bench said the Centre should study the verdict once again and accordingly call for information on each and every aspect of the matter. “On the next date of hearing, if we hear from the Union that some of the states/UTs have not responded, we shall proceed to issue contempt notice to the concerned chief secretary,” the bench said. While granting one last opportunity to do the needful, it posted the matter for next hearing on December 14. In its September 1 order, the bench had said the focus should be on the number of schools that lack gender-segregated, functional toilets with usable water connectivity, ensuring accessibility and privacy. The Centre had then informed the top court that 30,458 gender-segregated toilets with washing facilities have been constructed in schools across the country while 4,236 were under construction. In its judgment delivered in January, the apex court had directed the states and UTs to ensure that every school, whether government-run or privately managed, in both urban and rural areas, was provided with functional, gender-segregated toilets with usable water connectivity. The top court had also directed the states and UTs to ensure that every school provides sanitary napkins to girl students free of cost. The judgment was delivered on a plea seeking pan-India implementation of the Centre’s ‘menstrual hygiene policy for schoolgoing girls’ in government and government-aided schools from classes 6 to 12.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court gave states and Union territories a final chance to report compliance with its menstrual hygiene ruling.
Continued silence could invite contempt notices against the chief secretaries concerned.

The Supreme Court has expressed displeasure over states and Union territories not informing the Centre about the steps taken to implement its judgment declaring menstrual hygiene a part of the fundamental right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution, news agency Press Trust of India reported.

The court has given states and Union territories one last opportunity to provide the information, warning that it may issue contempt notices to the chief secretaries concerned if they fail to respond.
The next hearing is scheduled for December 14.

A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and R Mahadevan said, "If what we have said in the judgment is only going to remain on paper, how is the Union, states/UTs going to give effect to this fundamental right?"

In its January 30 judgment, the court had ruled that the constitutional right to life includes the right to menstrual health.
On September 1, it directed states and Union territories to consider the deficiencies highlighted in the judgment and submit reports by the next hearing.

At a hearing on October 13, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, told the bench that the Union government had taken up the matter seriously with all states and Union territories and sought details on how the judgment was being implemented, according to PTI.
Noting that no responses had been received, the bench said, "Unfortunately, the states/UTs have not responded to the Union so far.
We fail to understand that once the Union calls for the necessary information, why the states/UTs do not respond."

stories.headline: India voluntarily diversified energy portfolio: Rubio on Trump's tariff waiver
stories.title: India voluntarily diversified energy portfolio: Rubio on Trump's tariff waiver
stories.summary: India voluntarily diversified energy portfolio: Rubio on Trump's tariff waiver
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that President Donald Trump would take up to 60 days to assess the economic impact of the Russia-related sanctions and tariffs that were waived.

Day after United States President Donald Trump waived sanctions and tariffs related to Russian exports in a major relief to India and other countries, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington wanted more time to evaluate the situation.
He said on Saturday that the leader would use up to 60 days to assess the economic impact of the Russia-related sanctions and tariffs that were waived.
Rubio made the remarks while speaking to the press ahead of his departure for a six-day tour of Uzbekistan and India.
He said New Delhi had "voluntarily diversified" its fuel portfolio but was still getting a "substantial amount" of its energy imports from Russia as it is "hard" to change suppliers overnight.
Rubio said, "The problem is these sanctions were not just sanctions on Russia.
They include tariffs on a number of countries – India, for example, and others.
And so I think the President wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyze what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the US economy."

On Friday, Trump waived key provisions of the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, also known as the Graham Act, which authorised punitive levies on countries purchasing Russian oil, such as India and China.

Rubio said the law, which was passed on September 18, included provisions for waivers to allow the administration time to assess the impact of various global conflicts and their implications for energy supplies and prices.

"I think when the bill was passed, one of the reasons the waivers were put in there is the understanding that they would need some period of time to study this, given all the different things that are going on in the world right now, including the pressure on global energy supplies that are happening not just because of Iran, not just because of the Straits of Hormuz, but increasingly because of the Houthis attacking Saudi Arabia and because of the war with Ukraine and Russia, where energy infrastructure is being hit.
And so that’s having an impact on global prices as well," he said.

stories.headline: Supreme Court calls internet access a fundamental right for children, rejects blanket ban
stories.title: Supreme Court calls internet access a fundamental right for children, rejects blanket ban
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday, October 15, held that the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right of every individual, including children irrespective of their age.

A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said the right flows from Article 21, which guarantees the right to life and personal liberty, read with Article 19(1)(a), which protects freedom of speech and expression.

“We have no hesitation in saying that the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right of every individual under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution,” the court said in its 136-page order.

“Our children, irrespective of their age, enjoy the same rights, and to deny the same altogether would be as absurd as saying children below a certain age do not have a conscience worth protecting or a freedom of speech worth expressing.
The safety of our children and their freedom are not at odds with each other.
Our children are entitled to both,” it added.

The court was considering applications filed by the NGO Just Rights for Children Alliance in proceedings arising from its September 23, 2024 judgement, which dealt with the circulation of child sexual exploitation and abuse material online.
The organisation had raised concerns about continued lapses by social media intermediaries and other online platforms in complying with the earlier directions.
The bench expressed disappointment at the lack of meaningful progress in tackling the circulation of such material despite its judgement two years ago.
It added that recent reports placed before it had revealed “an even more unsettling reality” concerning the safety and wellbeing of children online.

The court noted that reports of paid promotions of Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material (CSEAM) through redirect links and websites were only a rare instance of such activities being detected and brought to light.

“There are millions more such incidents freely available on social media platforms that may never come to the knowledge of the proper authorities if no collective action is taken today by all stakeholders,” it said.

article_sentences: The story so far: A Supreme Court judgment on October 15 addressed the everyday anxiety of parents, who are torn between allowing their children access to the Internet and the need to keep them safe from vile, abusive online content.

The judgment by a Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran reasons that the solution is not to ban children from using the Internet, but to take measures to keep them safe from exploitation by predators lurking online.
The court declared that a child, like any other individual, has a fundamental right to access and use the Internet.
The State, lawmakers and parents cannot blame children for the presence of Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material (CSEAM) on the Internet.
The wrongdoer is the person who creates, circulates, sells or seeks out such material, and the intermediary which fails to detect and remove the content.
To keep the child away from the Internet on account of such failures would be to mistake the victim for the problem.
Any measure for the safety of children must be directed at the harmful material and those responsible for the same, and not at the children themselves.
The court held that “our children are entitled to both safety and the freedom to access the Internet”.
To deny them the freedom to go online would be as absurd as saying children below a certain age did not have a conscience worth protecting or a freedom of speech worth expressing.

The court found that its directions for online child safety in a September 23, 2024 judgment in a petition filed by Justice Rights for Children Alliance were largely ignored for the past two years, leading to serious lapses.
The court said there had been an “alarming increase” in child sexual exploitation and CSEAM circulated on social media platforms.

It flagged how indirect links to such harmful material were promoted and shared through social media algorithms to bypass the rigours of the special penal provisions designed for the protection of children within cyberspace.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Directs States, UTs To Notify Anti-Human Trafficking Units As Police Station
stories.title: Supreme Court Directs States, UTs To Notify Anti-Human Trafficking Units As Police Station
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has directed all States and Union Territories to take steps to confer police station status on Anti-Human Trafficking Units (ATHUs) by issuing appropriate notifications in accordance with law, emphasising that the measure is necessary for the effective implementation of its Victim Protection Plan to combat human trafficking.
A bench of Justice J.B. Pardiwala and Justice R. Mahadevan directed the Home Departments of all States and Union Territories to give effect to the direction at the earliest.
It also asked the Union Government to take up the issue with all States and UTs and ensure that the necessary notifications are issued.

The direction came during an ongoing hearing in which the Court reviewed compliance with its May 29, 2026 judgment concerning human trafficking of women and children for commercial sexual exploitation.

Senior Advocate Aparna Bhat, appearing for the petitioner, brought to the Court's attention that ATHUs needed to be given the status of police stations in accordance with paragraph 362(b)(iii) of the main judgment.

“In this regard, we direct all the State/UT Governments in their respective Home Departments to give effect to this direction at the earliest by issuing an appropriate notification, in accordance with law.”
The Court added that the Union Government “shall also take up this issue at the earliest with all the States/UTs and see to it that appropriate notifications are issued.”
The direction forms part of the Court's broader effort to ensure effective implementation of the Victim Protection Plan framed under Article 142 of the Constitution.
The bench noted that the four additional directions issued in paragraph 456 of its main judgment had not been fully complied with by all States and UTs.

These include notifying recognised welfare institutions under Sections 15(6A) and 17A of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956; preparing State- and UT-wide lists of eligible social welfare workers; and designating.
Police Nodal Officers and Government Nodal.
Officers.

stories.headline: India's GDP per capita catching up with richer nations, growth worth celebrating: Korean economist
stories.title: India's GDP per capita catching up with richer nations, growth worth celebrating: Korean economist
stories.summary: The economist pointed to India's rising per capita income and a sharp decline in poverty to argue that the country's economic transformation over the past three decades, particularly the last 10 years, deserves greater attention
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Kim, Head of the India and South Asia Team at the Korea Institute for International Economic Policy (KIEP), said on Sunday that his earlier assessment of India's medium-term growth prospects had attracted comments suggesting that India remained poor.
"A more useful question is whether living standards are rising rapidly and whether India is CATCHING UP," he wrote in a detailed post on X.
According to the figures shared by Kim, India's GDP per capita stood at $2,702 in 2025, or $11,784 when adjusted for purchasing power parity (PPP).
For historical comparisons, he used GDP per capita at constant 2021 PPP prices, which stood at $10,039 in 2025.
Kim noted that India was classified as a low-income country by the World Bank until 2007.
In 1990, India's GDP per capita was only 15% higher than the average for low-income countries.
By 2025, it had risen to more than four times that average.
The improvement was also visible when India was compared with middle-income economies, a group that includes fast-growing countries such as China and Vietnam.
India's GDP per capita reached 64% of the middle-income country average in 2025, with much of the catch-up taking place over the past decade.
Kim said India's progress against high-income economies had been more gradual but consistent.
In 1990, India's GDP per capita was just 6% of the high-income country average.
By 2025, that share had increased to 17%.
